definition: Neural Engine is a series of AI accelerators designed for machine learning by Apple.
details: Neural Engine was first introduced with the A11 Bionic system-on-a-chip (SoC), used in the iPhone 8, iPhone 8 Plus and iPhone X from 2017. In 2020, Apple introduced its M1 processor for its Mac computers which also used a Neural Engine. Every A-series and M-series processor since 2017 has included a Neural Engine. Apple services such as its Siri virtual assistant, Face ID facial recognition and Apple Intelligence AI services are powered by the Neural Engine, and since this is handled on-device, user data is secure.

explainer.lead: Neural Engine is a series of AI accelerators designed by Apple for machine learning. It powers on-device services like Siri and Face ID, enabling fast, private AI processing.

tiers.eli5: It's a special chip inside Apple devices that makes smart features like facial recognition work quickly without needing the internet.
tiers.practitioner: Developers leverage the Neural Engine via Apple's frameworks for on-device inference. A pitfall is that its capabilities are limited to supported operations and may require model optimization.
tiers.paperLevel: Neural Engine is a series of AI accelerators designed for machine learning by Apple. It was first introduced with the A11 Bionic SoC in 2017 and has been included in every A-series and M-series processor since.

explainer.example: The A11 Bionic chip in the iPhone X uses the Neural Engine to enable Face ID facial recognition.
